To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extracellular signal can be decomposed into a sum of sources, and that the sources of the extracellular field are synaptic transmembrane currents and the ionic currents through voltage- and ion-gated channels.
extracellular fields are a mixture of transmembrane currents from many neurons, and that the synaptic transmembrance current is the major contributor to the extracellular field.

the extracellular field potential is a complex signal that can be decomposed into several components that are generated by different neuronal sources and that have different spatial distributions and different time courses, that these components can be extracted by using different filtering techniques, and that the extracted components can be used for the analysis of the neuronal population activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of extracellular signals in the brain and how these signals relate to the underlying neuronal activity.
the origin and interpretation of extracellular field activity.
the generation, propagation, detection, processing, and interpretation of extracellular electrical signals from the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extracellular signal reflects neuronal activity, but the exact nature of this relationship remains to be elucidated.

the extracellular signal reflects neuronal spiking and synaptic currents, and that the relative contributions of these two processes depend on the frequency band and on the location of the recording site.
the extracellular signal represents the collective activity of the neuronal population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand the mechanisms that give rise to the extracellular field and to the extracellular current.
the brain is not a collection of independent neurons but a highly connected network where the neurons are constantly communicating with each other through electrical synapses and chemical synapses.

the extracellular signal reflects the average activity of the neuronal population, but that this activity depends on the spiking output of the neurons, which in turn is shaped by the synaptic input and intrinsic properties of the neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extracellular signal reflects the cooperative behaviour of many neurons.
extracellular fields and spikes can be considered as complementary signals that reflect the underlying neuronal activity.
, in the absence of synaptic inputs, the extracellular field is dominated by the transmembrane currents of the spiking neuron.
